page.text:
A relation $R$ on $X$ is *transitive* when connections bridge across
intermediate nodes:
$x \mathrel{R} y \land y \mathrel{R} z \implies x \mathrel{R} z$.
Transitivity is the algebraic guarantee that local relationships cohere
into global reachability.
